name: PixiTween Director E1: frame-exact MP4 export (browser renders, WebCodecs encodes, ffmpeg on the server as fallback and checker)
description: Adds a frame-exact MP4 export for any film, including the 3D hero films. The viewer's own browser seeks the film to every frame time and draws it with its GPU. Where WebCodecs H.264 is available, Mediabunny encodes the frames in the page (with the composition's audio). Where it is not, the page uploads JPEG frames to the server, which encodes them with ffmpeg (silent). The server also checks every finished MP4 with ffprobe for length, size, frame count and frozen frames. Judges install nothing: they open the deployed Fly app in Chrome and press Export. No Playwright, no headless Chromium, no CLI.

readFirst: web/src/export/mp4Export.ts, web/src/export/types.ts, web/src/export/playerCanvas.ts and web/src/panels/ExportPanel.tsx (the S8a export this makes frame-exact; today it plays in real time and samples)
web/src/player/Player.tsx (PlayerHandle: seek, getCanvas, whenReady) and web/src/dev/stage-check.tsx (seek then wait one animation frame before reading the canvas)

server/http/routes.ts (contract D-1), server/http/handlers/local.ts (handler module style), server/http/auth.ts (the passcode guards every non-GET route) and server/http/upload-limit.ts (hono bodyLimit)
web/src/api/client.ts (request() adds the passcode header on writes) and shared/api.ts (HealthResponse.ffmpeg)
server/authoring/motion-check.ts (changedShare, Gray) for the frozen-frame check
extraGuardrails: Reuse, never copy: runFfmpeg, hasFfmpeg, probeVideo, extractFrames and FfmpegMissingError come from server/media/ffmpeg.ts; changedShare comes from server/authoring/motion-check.ts. Do not edit either file.

Shared edits are small: server/http/routes.ts gets only the import and the registerExportRoutes(app, deps) line (the same exception C1 used); shared/api.ts gets only the export request and response types; README.md gets only one Export paragraph; docs/architecture/README.md gets only one link row. ExportPanel.tsx keeps its WebM path, its states and its aria labels.
No Playwright, no headless Chromium, no new npm dependency. Mediabunny is already installed. Frames are drawn by the viewer's browser only.

Tests never need a GPU or a real browser encoder: VideoEncoder, Mediabunny, canvas.toBlob and fetch are faked. The only real-ffmpeg tests are skipped when hasFfmpeg() is false and build their frames with sharp or ffmpeg lavfi testsrc.
The export never calls Muse, SAM, Meta or any model and spends nothing.
The server path is silent (no audio track). The browser path keeps the audio S8a already mixes.
Server export sessions live only in a temp dir under os.tmpdir() and are deleted on finish, on error and after 10 minutes idle. Nothing is written to the data folder.
The dev server on http://localhost:5173 is owner-run and shared: never kill or restart it. Real browser exports are manual gates.
manualGates: MG-1 (Chrome, local): open a 3D hero film at http://localhost:5173/?replay=1, choose MP4 and export. Play it in QuickTime and Chrome: same camera moves as the player, audio in sync by eye, no frozen stretch. Note the time taken and file size.

MG-2 (server path): in Chrome devtools run `delete window.VideoEncoder` (or use Firefox), reload, export MP4 again. The panel must say it is using the server; the file must play and be silent. Note the upload time and size.

MG-3 (Fly, after the owner deploys): open the deployed app in a browser with no local ffmpeg, export one film by each path, and confirm GET /api/health reports ffmpeg true. Timings in the doc are filled in from MG-1 to MG-3; until then they are estimates.
MG-4: compare frames at 1 s, 4 s and 7 s of the MP4 against the player paused at those times; flat cut-out products must show the same turn.

stories.title: ffmpeg encode helper: a folder of numbered frames to an H.264 MP4
stories.description: As a server maintainer, I want one function that turns numbered JPEG or PNG frames into a web-safe MP4 so that every server export uses the same encoder settings.
steps: Read server/media/ffmpeg.ts (runFfmpeg, hasFfmpeg, probeVideo) and server/media/ffmpeg.test.ts for how real runs are skipped.
Create server/media/encode.ts exporting frameName(i: number, ext: 'jpg' | 'png' = 'jpg'): string returning `f${String(i).padStart(5,'0')}.${ext}`.

Export buildEncodeArgs({ framesDir, fps, out, ext = 'jpg', crf = 18 }): string[] returning ['-y','-framerate',String(fps),'-i',`${framesDir}/f%05d.${ext}`,'-c:v','libx264','-pix_fmt','yuv420p','-crf',String(crf),'-preset','veryfast','-vf','scale=trunc(iw/2)*2:trunc(ih/2)*2:in_range=full:out_range=tv,format=yuv420p','-movflags','+faststart',out].

Export encodeFrames(o: { framesDir; fps; out; ext?; crf? }, run = runFfmpeg): Promise<void> that rejects with Error('no frames in <dir>') when f00000.<ext> is missing, and otherwise calls run(buildEncodeArgs(o), { timeoutMs: 300000 }).

Create server/media/encode.test.ts with a fake run for the pure parts, and one real-ffmpeg test (describe.skipIf(!(await hasFfmpeg()))) that writes 12 solid-colour 64x64 JPEGs with sharp (each a different colour), encodes them at 12 fps into a temp file and asserts probeVideo gives width 64, height 64 and frames 12.
acceptance: frameName(0) === 'f00000.jpg', frameName(239) === 'f00239.jpg' and frameName(3, 'png') === 'f00003.png'
buildEncodeArgs({ framesDir: 'd', fps: 30, out: 'o.mp4' }) contains 'd/f%05d.jpg', '-pix_fmt','yuv420p' and '-movflags','+faststart' and ends with 'o.mp4'; crf 23 changes only the crf value
encodeFrames on an empty temp dir rejects with a message containing 'no frames' and the fake run is called 0 times; with 3 frame files it is called once with the built args
The real-ffmpeg test yields an MP4 probed at 64x64 with 12 frames, or is skipped when ffmpeg is missing
The real-ffmpeg test also asserts the MP4's pix_fmt is yuv420p with limited (tv) range, not yuvj420p

stories.title: Check a finished MP4 against the film it came from
stories.description: As a viewer, I want every finished MP4 checked for length, size, frame count and frozen frames so that a broken export is reported instead of handed over silently.
steps: Read server/media/ffmpeg.ts (probeVideo, extractFrames) and server/authoring/motion-check.ts (changedShare, Gray).
Create server/media/export-check.ts exporting the type ExportExpect = { durationSec: number; fps: number; width: number; height: number }.

Export compareProbe(probe: { durationSec; width; height; frames }, expect: ExportExpect, tol = 0.15): string[] (pure): 'duration A s, expected B s' (two decimals) when they differ by more than tol; 'size WxH, expected WxH' when width or height differ by more than 1 (the encoder rounds odd sizes down); 'frames N, expected M' when the count differs by more than 2 from round(durationSec * fps).
Export frozenPairs(grays: Gray[], times: number[]): string[] (pure) returning 'frozen: frames at A s and B s are identical' for each neighbour pair whose changedShare is 0.

Export checkExport(video: Buffer, expect, deps = { probeVideo, extractFrames }): Promise<string[]>: probe and compareProbe, then extract 9 evenly spaced frames, reduce each to a 54x96 gray image with sharp and append frozenPairs. An ffmpeg failure returns ['check failed: <message>'] and never throws.

Create server/media/export-check.test.ts for compareProbe and frozenPairs with plain objects, checkExport with fake deps, and one real-ffmpeg test (skipped without ffmpeg) on a 2 s lavfi testsrc clip that returns no problems against its own expectation.
acceptance: compareProbe of a 6 s probe against an expected 8 s returns exactly ['duration 6.00 s, expected 8.00 s']
compareProbe returns [] for a probe within 0.15 s, 1 px and 2 frames of the expectation
frozenPairs with exactly one identical neighbour pair returns one problem starting with 'frozen:' that names both times
checkExport with a fake probeVideo that throws resolves to one problem starting with 'check failed:'
The real testsrc clip checks clean, or the test is skipped when ffmpeg is missing

stories.title: Server export routes: upload frames, encode with ffmpeg, check any MP4
stories.description: As a browser without WebCodecs, I want to upload my frames and get an MP4 back so that every viewer can export; and as any browser, I want the server to check my MP4.
steps: Read server/http/handlers/local.ts (handler module style), server/http/routes.ts, server/http/auth.ts and server/http/upload-limit.ts.
Add to shared/api.ts: ExportStartRequest { fps: number; frames: number; width: number; height: number }, ExportStartResponse { id: string }, ExportCheckResponse { problems: string[] }.

Create server/http/handlers/exports.ts exporting registerExportRoutes(app, deps, opts: { encode?; check?; hasFfmpeg?; now?; tmpRoot? } = {}) with: POST /api/exports (zod: fps 1..60, frames 1..1800, width and height 16..2160) -> 201 { id }, creating a temp dir; PUT /api/exports/:id/frames/:i (body image/jpeg, at most 4 MB through hono bodyLimit, i within 0..frames-1) -> 204, written as frameName(i); POST /api/exports/:id/finish -> encodes, runs checkExport, deletes the dir, and answers 200 with the MP4 bytes (content-type video/mp4) and an 'x-export-problems' header holding the JSON array; POST /api/exports/check (body video/mp4, at most 200 MB, query durationSec, fps, width, height) -> 200 ExportCheckResponse.

Errors: 503 { error: 'ffmpeg_missing' } on every route when hasFfmpeg() is false; 404 { error: 'no_such_export' } for an unknown id; 409 { error: 'missing_frames', missing: number[] } on finish when any frame was not uploaded (the first 20 indexes); 429 { error: 'busy' } when 2 sessions are already open. A session idle for 10 minutes is deleted on the next request.
Add the import and registerExportRoutes(app, deps) line to server/http/routes.ts after registerLocalRoutes; change nothing else there.

Create server/http/handlers/exports.test.ts on a bare Hono app with fake encode and check and a temp tmpRoot: the start, frames and finish flow; each error above; idle expiry with a fake now(); the dir is gone after finish and after an encode error. Add one real-ffmpeg test (skipped without ffmpeg) that uploads 6 sharp JPEGs and gets back bytes that probeVideo reads as 6 frames.
acceptance: start, 3 frame PUTs and finish answer 201, 204 x3 and 200 with content-type video/mp4, and the fake encode was called once
finish with frame 1 of 3 missing answers 409 with missing [1]; an unknown id answers 404; a third open session answers 429
with hasFfmpeg faked false every export route answers 503 { error: 'ffmpeg_missing' }
a PUT of a 5 MB body answers 413 and writes nothing
the session temp dir no longer exists after finish, after a failed encode and after idle expiry
POST /api/exports without the passcode answers 401 when a passcode is configured (through the app's middleware chain)
server/http/routes.ts differs from before only by the import and the one register line

stories.title: Frame-exact capture in the browser and WebCodecs MP4 encode
stories.description: As a viewer, I want the MP4 built from exactly one frame per frame time so that 3D camera moves are smooth and nothing is dropped, however slow my machine is.
steps: Read web/src/export/mp4Export.ts (the real-time version this does not delete), web/src/export/types.ts, web/src/export/playerCanvas.ts and web/src/dev/stage-check.tsx (seek, then one animation frame).

Create web/src/export/frameExport.ts exporting frameTimes(durationSec, fps): number[] (i / fps for i = 0 .. ceil(durationSec * fps) - 1, rounded to 4 decimals) and settle(raf = requestAnimationFrame): Promise<void> resolving after two animation frames.

Export captureFrames(o: { driver: ExportDriver; durationSec; fps; signal?; onFrame(i, timeSec): Promise<void>; onProgress? }, deps = { settle }): Promise<number>: pause the driver, then for each time seek, await settle(), await onFrame(i, t) and report progress; throws ExportError('aborted') when the signal aborts between frames; returns the frame count. It never calls play().

Export exportMp4Exact(o: { canvas; driver; durationSec; fps?; audio?; onProgress?; signal? }, deps = { mediabunny?, settle? }): Promise<Blob> building Output(Mp4OutputFormat, BufferTarget), a CanvasSource(canvas, { codec: 'avc', quality: Quality('high') }) and, when audio is given, an AudioBufferSource({ codec: 'aac' }); it uses captureFrames with onFrame = videoSource.add(t, 1 / fps), then adds the audio, finalizes and returns a video/mp4 Blob.
Create web/src/export/frameExport.test.ts with a fake driver that records calls, a settle that resolves at once and vi.mock('mediabunny') as in mp4Export.test.ts.
acceptance: frameTimes(8, 30) has 240 entries, starts at 0 and ends at 7.9667; frameTimes(1, 24) has 24
captureFrames over 1 s at 24 fps seeks exactly 24 times in increasing order, awaits settle before each onFrame, and never calls play()
aborting the signal after frame 5 rejects with ExportError code 'aborted' and onFrame was called 6 times or fewer
exportMp4Exact calls videoSource.add 240 times for 8 s at 30 fps with timestamps i/30 and duration 1/30, adds an AudioBufferSource only when audio is passed, and returns a Blob of type 'video/mp4'

stories.title: Browser client for the server path: upload JPEG frames, check any MP4
stories.description: As a viewer in a browser without WebCodecs H.264, I want my frames sent to the server for encoding so that I still get an MP4.
steps: Read web/src/api/client.ts (request() and the passcode header) and the routes from US-003.

Create web/src/export/serverExport.ts exporting exportMp4ViaServer(o: { canvas; driver; durationSec; fps?; onProgress?; signal? }, deps = { request?, settle?, toJpeg? }): Promise<{ blob: Blob; problems: string[] }>. It POSTs /api/exports, uses captureFrames with onFrame = toJpeg(canvas, 0.9) then PUT /api/exports/<id>/frames/<i>, and finally POSTs finish and reads the x-export-problems header. Uploads run at most 4 at a time; progress is frames uploaded / total.
Use fetch with the same passcode header as request() for the binary bodies (export a small helper from serverExport.ts; do not edit client.ts).
Export checkMp4OnServer(blob, expect): Promise<string[]> that POSTs /api/exports/check and returns problems, or [] with no error shown when the server answers 503 (no ffmpeg there).

Map server errors to ExportError: 503 ffmpeg_missing -> code 'unsupported' with the message 'This server has no ffmpeg, so it cannot build an MP4 for this browser.'; 429 busy -> message 'The server is busy with another export. Try again in a minute.'
Create web/src/export/serverExport.test.ts with a fake fetch and toJpeg.
acceptance: a 1 s, 6 fps export makes 1 start request, 6 frame PUTs with content-type image/jpeg and the passcode header, and 1 finish request, and never has more than 4 PUTs in flight
the returned problems equal the parsed x-export-problems header
a 503 from start rejects with ExportError code 'unsupported' and the ffmpeg message
checkMp4OnServer resolves [] on a 503 and the parsed problems on a 200
